hypothesis_or_artifact: H2, the age-contrast pair - Amendment H2-4 section 4, the look-1 futility boundary and the n2 it is computed against

So E1's futility boundary is computed against a look-2 sample the design will never have; E1 will be judged at look 2 on 117 pairs at minimum. Conditional power increases in n2 - n1, so understating n2 inflates f1 and makes the terminal FAIL fire on more outcomes; for E2 the registered n2 coincides with the governing figure, so the defect is E1-specific and E1 is the leg whose f1 moves most. Direction is not stated for this choice in a document that states direction for every other one (registrations/H2/REGISTRATION.md:441, 451; registrations/H5/REGISTRATION.md:417-418, 517) - the one choice that tightens a terminal stop carries no direction statement.

hypothesis_or_artifact: H2 - Amendment H2-3 Change 2 / ADR-023, the retirement of the 2x economic floor (co-primary E2) to a named secondary, and the calendar argument that carried it
label: DERIVED
claim_quote: The alternative considered and declined: keep 2x and accept a 169-pair single-look minimum reached near 2027-05/06, past the registered deadline. That is not a stricter experiment, it is an experiment that never reports.

hypothesis_or_artifact: HYPOTHESES.md - the register index's reopen conditions for H3 and H4, against the registrations they summarise
label: READ
claim_quote: Reopens only on an order-of-magnitude higher main-dex listing rate or a longer-horizon successor registration
evidence_summary: H3's registration lists three reopeners and the index drops one: 'What would reopen it: a main-dex listing rate near 40-50/month sustained (min-N 262 against 0.5/month measured), a register deadline years longer, or a successor registration on a different venue whose main-population listing rate supports the bars' (registrations/H3/REGISTRATION.md:184-188). The index's word is 'only', and the clause it drops - a different venue - is the cheapest and most actionable of the three. The index's quantity is also wrong by a factor of about 8: an order of magnitude on 0.5/month is 5/month, yielding about 35 main-dex events by 2027-03-31 against a P1 minimum N of 262 (min_n_for_080.'H3/P1'.'k=1'.min_n = 262 in reports/stage_a_h2/ktable_cull.json); 262 events over the 7.06 months to the deadline needs about 37/month, which is the registration's own 40-50/month. The same narrowing happens for H4, more severely: the registration gives three clauses (registrations/H4/REGISTRATION.md:230-234) and HYPOTHESES.md:106 gives one, dropping the only one that can fire. This matters because of what the index is for in its own words - 'Read this before proposing any new hypothesis on new-listing drift.' (HYPOTHESES.md:3) and 'The failure mode this file exists to prevent is retrying a settled question because the number that closed it is buried.' (HYPOTHESES.md:32-33). No reopen trigger has been met by a later entry in this repository: the two measured rates that gate H3 and H4 (0.5 main-dex events/month, n = 3 in 182 days, registrations/H3/REGISTRATION.md:161-163; conditioning 0.1774/0.1290/0.0806, n = 62, registrations/H4/REGISTRATION.md:210-212) have no later re-measurement anywhere in the snapshot.
recomputation: Arithmetic from figures printed in the documents: 5 events/month x 7.06 months = 35.3 against a min-N of 262; 262/7.06 = 37.1 events/month required, against the registration's 40-50/month and the index's implied 5/month.
would_resolve: Carry all three registered reopen clauses verbatim into each index row - or replace 'Reopens only on ...' with a pointer to the registration's own clause - and correct H3's index wording from 'order-of-magnitude higher' to the registration's 40-50/month.
confidence_why: Both texts are quoted in full, the mismatch is exact, and the arithmetic uses the register's own min-N.
invalidation_note: Both entries are BLOCKED with nothing armed; an index edit would fix rather than invalidate the finding.

hypothesis_or_artifact: H3, the population-corrected naive short - the magnitude co-primary's governing assumption, and the stratified figure the single permitted read did not compute
label: DERIVED
claim_quote: - **H3: BLOCKED.** Measured main-dex accrual 0.5/month (n = 3/182d) against the falsified ~9.4 planning figure; deadline N = 5 vs P1 min-N 262; powers 0.0000 / 0.0057 (0.1160 at the optimistic 0.65, beside).
evidence_summary: The magnitude leg is unpowerable at any n on any venue at any listing rate, because its governing assumption sits below the null it is tested against: 'H3/MAG': {'k=1': {'min_n': null, 'note': 'governing true share at or below the null: no n reaches 0.80'}} in reports/stage_a_h2/ktable_cull.json (min_n_for_080), with requirement mode 'all - P1 and MAG are both required and the weaker governs the cull' (registrations/H3/REGISTRATION.md:102-103). So H3's BLOCKED does not depend on the main-dex accrual measurement at all: it is entailed by the assumption choice alone, while both closure summaries present it as an accrual result (progress.md:691-693; HYPOTHESES.md:89). That governing figure was taken pooled because a stratified one was believed not to exist ('magnitude share unknown - no subset figure exists', HYPOTHESES.md:92; 'the H1 measured overall 0.356', registrations/H3/REGISTRATION.md:87). But the spent read did stratify by exactly H3's population split for the other statistic: per_type_strata_30d = {hip3: {n: 154, share_positive: 0.5844}, hyperp_conversion: {n: 46, 0.6957}, vanilla: {n: 112, 0.6696}} in reports/stage_b/read.json, and there is no per-type magnitude figure anywhere in that artifact. The registered secondary is stated without restriction to one statistic - 'Named secondaries, descriptive: the 90-day versions, strata by vanilla, hyperp_conversion, and hip3, ...' (progress.md:412, the registered Stage B.2 Task 1 text; 'per-type strata' likewise in REGISTRATION.md Section 8) - so had the magnitude statistic been stratified in the one read that was permitted, H3's governing assumption would have been a measured main-dex number rather than a pooled one; the quarantine now forbids computing it (ADR-014, DECISIONS.md:166-177). The direction is not neutral: on the statistic that was stratified the main-dex strata are the stronger half (vanilla 0.6696 n = 112, hyperp_conversion 0.6957 n = 46, pooled main-dex 107/158 = 0.677) against hip3 0.5844 n = 154 and pooled 0.631, and H3's own P1 assumption uses exactly that main-dex stratification. Only the magnitude leg was left pooled, and the magnitude leg governs.
recomputation: Inputs: MAG governing share 0.356 (111/312 - reports/stage_b/read.json co_primaries.p2.successes/n); exact one-sided sign test against 1/2 at alpha 0.016952 and 0.05; P1 main-dex share 0.677 (107/158) with the Clopper-Pearson lower bound against 0.60; measured main-dex accrual 0.5/month (n = 3 in 182 days, docs/ACCESS.md:265-266). Method: exact binomial power sweeps. Result: MAG power at 0.356 is 1.20e-05 at n = 50, 7.72e-19 at n = 500, 6.19e-117 at n = 5000 - monotonically falling because the assumed share is below the null, so no n reaches any power, reproducing the artifact's note exactly. P1: the smallest n from which power stays >= 0.80 is 262 (the CP boundary is non-monotone; the first single crossing is 248), reproducing the registered figure. Scripts: scratchpad/work/agentA-NPL-p2/calc.py sections 3, 4, 6 and calc2.py.
would_resolve: State the closure as 'BLOCKED by the magnitude assumption at any n' rather than as an accrual result, and record that the main-dex magnitude share was inside the registered scope of the per-type-strata secondary and was not computed by the single permitted read - so a successor register knows the assumption is a pooled stand-in, not a measurement of the population H3 tests.
confidence_why: The arithmetic is exact and the artifact's own note confirms it; whether the registered 'per-type strata' secondary obliged the read to stratify the magnitude statistic as well as the share-positive one is a reading of the registration the authors could reasonably dispute.
invalidation_note: HEAD equals the anchor, H3 is closed with nothing armed, and the read is spent and quarantined, so the stratified figure can no longer be computed.
disclosure_ref: Partially disclosed, and in the other reader's documents: 'the magnitude leg at its governing share reaches 0.80 at no n' and 'the verdict is insensitive to the k/alpha question and to the magnitude-leg assumption' (registrations/H3/REGISTRATION.md:171-177). Not disclosed anywhere: that the stratified magnitude figure was within the registered scope of the spent read and was not computed, or that the strata which were computed run in the direction that would have raised the assumption.

label: READ
claim_quote: **Nothing reopens H1 itself** - the registered short does not clear its bars on this sample, and the sample is spent.
evidence_summary: H1's hypothesis is stated over two horizons - 'earns a positive net return over 30 and 90 days' (REGISTRATION.md:53-55; identically HYPOTHESES.md:44-46, README.md:21-23, progress.md:10, CLAUDE.md:8-10) - with Section 7 making 30 days primary and 90 days secondary (REGISTRATION.md:188). At 90 days the profitability co-primary clears its registered bar: '90-day versions (descriptive): share positive 208/312 = 66.67 percent, lower bound 0.6069' against the 0.60 bar (REGISTRATION.md:570-571, 206), and P3 clears at p = 2.36e-04 (111/175); the same figures are in reports/stage_b/read.json (secondaries.horizon_90d_co_primaries: p1 passes true, p2 passes false at 159/312, p3 passes true). Only the magnitude leg fails, and as a null rather than a rejection: 159/312 = 0.5096 is on the hypothesis side of one half at p = 0.3886, against the 30-day 111/312 at p = 1.000. The register row, the closure entry and the README carry only the 30-day figures (HYPOTHESES.md:52; REGISTRATION.md:600-602; README.md:6-10). No successor carries the horizon: H2 is '30 days primary, 90 days secondary (descriptive)' (registrations/H2/REGISTRATION.md:141), H3 likewise (registrations/H3/REGISTRATION.md:65-66), H4 carries H1 Sections 3, 4, 7 verbatim (registrations/H4/REGISTRATION.md:85-87), the outcome-blind cull scored exactly three 30-day designs (report.md:362-367), and no power number for any 90-day variant appears anywhere; the stage ladder marks the question void with the row (docs/STAGES.md:71). recomputation: Inputs: 208/312, 159/312, 111/175 (REGISTRATION.md:570-572; verified identical in reports/stage_b/read.json secondaries.horizon_90d_co_primaries); alpha_adj 0.016952 (REGISTRATION.md:201); bar 0.60; accrual 18.57 events/month and 135 readable fresh events by 2027-03-31 (report.md:340-341, 561). Method: exact Clopper-Pearson lower bound; exact one-sided sign tests; exact binomial power at p0 = 0.60. Result: 90-day P1 lower bound 0.606866 (document 0.6069) and 0.62011 at alpha 0.05 - clears at both; P2-90d p = 0.388589 with share 0.50962; P3-90d p = 2.3605e-04. Against the thesis, twice: (i) the registered table would still have fired FAIL at 90 days, since FAIL is 'P1 or P2 fails' and P2 would need 176 of 312 to clear alpha_adj against 159 observed; (ii) a fresh 90-day profitability-only successor would not have survived the cull - at the generating-sample 90-day share 0.6667 and 135 projected readable fresh events, power is 0.2635 (k = 3) / 0.3270 (k = 2) / 0.4677 (k = 1), under the 0.50 BLOCKED floor, reaching 0.80 only at 347 events, about 18 months of accrual, about 2028-03. Scripts: scratchpad/work/agentA-NPL-p1/recompute*.py; agentA-NPL-p2/calc.py section 5 and calc3.py.
would_resolve: Put the 90-day row into the register index's H1 entry beside the 30-day row - that at the registration's own secondary horizon P1 cleared (208/312, lb 0.6069, n = 312) and P3 cleared at p = 2.4e-04 while the magnitude leg still failed - and replace 'Nothing reopens H1 itself' with the deadline-bounded version the arithmetic supports ('a 90-day successor needs about 347 fresh events, about 2028-03 at the measured accrual'), the same form as H3's registered 'a register deadline years longer'.
confidence_why: The numbers are certain and reproduce exactly and the successor set is certain; the weight of the finding is a documentation and reopen-condition judgement, since the fired row is mechanically correct either way.
invalidation_note: H1 is closed and its read is spent and quarantined; only an edit to the register index could change it.
disclosure_ref: Yes, in part, and the severity is capped at S3 because of it: report.md:233-235 reports the 90-day lower bound and adds '(would sit above 0.60 - descriptive only)', and REGISTRATION.md:570-572 carries the same figures inside the verdict record. Not disclosed: that the register index, the closure entry and the README carry none of it while asserting unconditional non-reopening, and that no 90-day successor was ever scored.

hypothesis_or_artifact: H5 - the retrospective branch declared absent, and the one-venue constraint (ADR-027) stated as a fact about the world rather than about this entry's registered scope
label: READ
claim_quote: **No retrospective basis exists.** The venue serves no historical mark and no historical oracle in the same row, and `candleSnapshot` is closed to this entry by standing rule 7.
evidence_summary: Half of the stated reason is a self-imposed rule, not a data-availability fact: 'a candle read with a price is a rule-7 violation. So Task 3's retrospective series can come only from a venue-served field that carries a deviation directly' (registrations/H5/REGISTRATION.md:41-45; DECISIONS.md:530-533). The venue does serve historical candles - the H1 collectors sealed 312 event windows and 176 control windows from candleSnapshot (report.md:74-77) with measured-full retention (report.md:334-338). The other half of the reference is available from outside the venue, and the registration names it as exactly what is needed (registrations/H5/REGISTRATION.md:195-197, 328-330). The entry's registered spend rule does not forbid it: standing rule 9 is 'Zero dollars. Keyless public endpoints only.' (CLAUDE.md:40-41; registrations/H5/REGISTRATION.md:286-288), constraining cost and credentials, not venue count; of the three grounds at DECISIONS.md:417-418 ('zero dollars, keyless endpoints, one venue') only the third is a genuine restriction, and what actually forbids an external reference is a scope sentence, 'This entry reads no external equity price feed.' (registrations/H5/REGISTRATION.md:174). The repository has already fetched from a non-venue HTTP source when it needed a documented figure (docs/ACCESS.md:95-98), so the machinery and precedent for a keyless off-venue read exist. Consequence with its n: the retrospective half of the entry's question is answered by absence rather than measurement, and the entry instead waits 29 daily passes for a forward census over 94 live instruments (HYPOTHESES.md:126; report.md:659) whose reference is the venue's own - which the same ADR says 'measures the venue's bookkeeping, not a tradable gap' (DECISIONS.md:425-426) - so the best row this entry can produce authorizes only work in another repository. The properly qualified form exists in the repository and is not the one the index carries: 'A retrospective basis of the registered construction does not exist.' (report.md:644); HYPOTHESES.md:128 drops 'of the registered construction', and HYPOTHESES.md is the file a reader is told to consult first (HYPOTHESES.md:3). No unverified external endpoint is asserted as evidence: the drafts' named keyless feeds were dropped at consolidation for want of a file:line, a figure and an n.
would_resolve: Cheapest and sufficient for honesty: restate the claim as 'no retrospective basis is available within this entry's registered scope' wherever it appears unqualified, notably HYPOTHESES.md:128, matching report.md:644. Optionally, record why an external keyless zero-dollar reference is excluded when standing rule 9 excludes only cost and keys, or admit one as a registered secondary comparison for the large-cap subset so a VIABLE row could mean something inside this repository.
confidence_why: The scope decision is deliberate, argued at length and internally consistent, and the authors may hold 'one venue' as a boundary independent of the spend rule, in which case there is no defect, only a cost worth recording. The finding is that the summary states a scope fact as a fact about the world.
invalidation_note: H5 is live until 2026-09-26 and an amendment or an index edit would moot it; no commit after the anchor existed at read time.
disclosure_ref: Yes, and the severity is capped at S3 because of it: the reason is given in the same sentence at HYPOTHESES.md:128, in full at registrations/H5/REGISTRATION.md:38-45 and 174-197, and the properly qualified form is stated at report.md:644; DECISIONS.md:424-434 discloses the epistemic consequence at length and pre-registers that a near-zero basis is the likely measurement. This is a wording/scope objection, not a discovery. Not recorded anywhere: that the constraint is stricter than standing rule 9 requires, and that a keyless free external reference was never considered.
